claims.text: Quenching Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 from its homogenization temperature produces a homogeneous, disordered BCC initial state.
The stability of the high-temperature BCC phase in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is controlled by an Al-induced thermodynamic driving force for ordering.
At a critical temperature, the ordering driving force overcomes sluggish atomic mobility.
Overcoming the kinetic constraint nucleates ordered intermetallic domains, such as B2, and destabilizes the original BCC matrix.
Controlled isothermal aging around the predicted ordering temperature will induce temperature- and time-dependent phase evolution.
The relevant structural mediator is the formation and growth of nanometer-scale ordered B2-like domains or precipitates inside a disordered BCC matrix.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the disordered BCC phase at high temperature.
At intermediate temperatures, Al increases the thermodynamic instability of the disordered state.
Thermal activation permits sufficient atomic diffusion for ordering despite sluggish-diffusion constraints.
The balance between the entropy contribution and the ordering driving force establishes a critical temperature above which pronounced ordered precipitation occurs.
Samples aged above the critical temperature will exhibit an increased ordered-phase fraction.
Samples aged above the critical temperature will exhibit growth of ordered precipitates.
Ordered precipitation will produce measurable lattice-parameter changes.
Ordered precipitation will alter mechanical properties, potentially increasing hardness or embrittlement.
Samples aged below the critical temperature will largely retain a metastable disordered BCC state.
The proposed mechanism operates only in a temperature window where diffusion is sufficient for ordering and the alloy remains below melting.
Very low temperatures suppress ordering through insufficient diffusion, while temperatures near melting fall outside the proposed regime because equilibrium may be re-established.
The critical ordering temperature and quantitative nucleation and growth kinetics for Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 are unknown because alloy-specific thermodynamic data are limited.

Failure to observe a statistically significant increase in ordered-phase fraction or associated microstructural and mechanical changes above the predicted critical temperature relative to the as-quenched baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says that decreasing temperature reduces the entropy stabilization of disorder and increases the driving force for ordering, but it defines pronounced precipitation as occurring above a critical temperature and predicts that samples below it retain disordered BCC. This reverses the usual thermodynamic direction of an ordering temperature unless the stated threshold is explicitly defined as a kinetic lower bound rather than a thermodynamic ordering transition.
